caption: A rod sample with its flame shrunk to a small blue cap facing the incoming air. BASS-II describes rod flames taking this hemispherical blue shape just before they go out.
A rod burning with the air flowing along it: a blue leading edge, then a long yellow flame trailing downstream inside the flow duct. Taken in early 2016, when BASS-II ran its last rod tests.
A PMMA sphere with a bright, sooty flame streaming downstream. BASS burned 1 and 2 cm PMMA spheres in spring 2013. Soot like this is fuel that did not finish burning.
A weak flame that has turned almost entirely blue, the near-extinction look the BASS-II report describes as flow or oxygen drops. The fuel is hidden behind the flame.
A gas flame on ACME's coflow burner, blue with a small yellow soot tip. Taken on Oct 18, 2018, during the E-FIELD Flames run, which tested how electric fields push on flames.

A dome-shaped flame over the flat porous burner of the Burning Rate Emulator, which feeds gas through its surface to imitate a burning solid. In still air these flames went out on their own below about 25% O2.
An ethylene flame wrapped around ACME's spherical porous burner, glowing yellow-orange with soot and scattered with bright specks.
A spherical flame with a bright blue edge and a dim orange soot glow inside, from the same burner later that day. Flame Design looked for conditions that make flames burn without soot.
